reports.title: REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS INCLUDING RECORD OIL PRODUCTION AND CONTINUED DEBT REPAYMENT

guidance.heading: Full-Year 2026 Guidance Update
section: Effective November 3, 2026, Matador increased its full-year 2026 guidance range for oil, natural gas and total BOE production as set forth in the table below.

Guidance Metric | February Full-Year 2026 Guidance Range | August Full-Year 2026Guidance Range(3) | Current Full-Year 2026Guidance Range(3)
Oil Production, Bbl per day | 122,000 to 124,000 | 127,500 to 129,000 | 128,750 to 129,250
Natural Gas Production, MMcf per day | 525.0 to 545.0 | 546.0 to 567.0 | 565.5 to 568.5
Total Oil Equivalent Production, BOE per day | 209,500 to 215,000 | 218,500 to 223,500 | 223,000 to 224,000
Current income taxes (% of pretax income) | 0% to 0.5% | 0% to 1% | 0% to 1%
D/C/E CapEx(1) | $1.35 to $1.44 billion | $1.48 to $1.56 billion | $1.50 to $1.54 billion
Midstream CapEx(2) | $100 to $110 million | $145 to $165 million | $170 to $190 million
Total CapEx | $1.45 to $1.55 billion | $1.625 to $1.725 billion | $1.67 to $1.73 billion

(1) Capital expenditures associated with drilling, completing and equipping wells. Includes 107.6 net operated wells in February full-year 2026 guidance and increased to 112.6 net operated wells in current full-year 2026 guidance.

(2) Includes Matador’s share of estimated capital expenditures for San Mateo and other wholly-owned midstream projects. Includes the expansion of the Marlan processing plant and pipeline build outs to connect to properties adjacent to acreage acquired in the recent Federal lease sale. Excludes acquisition costs.
(3) Includes production associated with the Paloma and Ridge Runner acquisitions that closed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Includes the Cardinal Midstream acquisition, which closed on July 31, 2026.

Matador raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 production guidance to the high end of its prior full-year 2026 production range previously provided on August 5, 2026 based on market conditions. This new midpoint represents 7% production growth from year end 2025. In view of Matador’s growing acreage position, similar to 2026, Matador estimates it could deliver mid-single digit growth or better in full-year 2027 as compared to full-year 2026 based on current commodity pricing and oilfield service costs. Matador’s expected 2026 production from 221,000 BOE per day to 223,500 BOE per day is attributable to:
•1,600 BOE per day from better-than-expected production in the third quarter of 2026 as detailed below and
•900 BOE per day from improvements to expected production in the fourth quarter of 2026.
